description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06).  BISECTED.  NOT FIXED HERE.

THE NUMBER.  baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv carried `run/fresh_perl.t 91 0 59 32
XDIFF` -- blessed at 3016011e (s469bf, which had just won two rows).  It now
reads **C 0/0 DIFF**: the file produces no TAP at all, so 59 rows that used to
PASS are simply not there.  That is invisible to the count comparison the
companion prints per file (0/0 is one line) and is exactly the shortfall
instrument's reason for existing; the row is in baselines/row-shortfall.tsv as
`t/run/fresh_perl.t 91`.

BISECTED over 3016011e..614c6af (55 commits, 4 binary-search steps, each a
`git checkout --detach` in a temp worktree + `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1
run/fresh_perl.t`):

    3016011e ... 0d1b5c18   C 59/32     (index 20 of the range: GOOD)
    9d43ccf2                C  0/0      (index 21: FIRST BAD)
    97de8d18, 614c6af, 424cabc, HEAD    C 0/0

**9d43ccf2 = s470bk (Opus): #1057 -- "a compound assign to a nested element
vivifies its container, through the walker p-setf already uses"**
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp +200/-76, Pl/t/autoviv-02.t +41).

THE SYMPTOM.  The runner's normalised abort signature is

    aborted-forms:1: Invalid index -N for (vector t N), should be a
    non-negative integer below N.

i.e. a NEGATIVE index reaching a raw CL vector accessor.  #1057 routed compound
assignment to a nested element through the p-setf container walker; something in
that walker hands a negative subscript straight to the vector op instead of
resolving it against the array length the way the read path does.  A negative
index is ordinary Perl (`$a[-1] .= "x"`), so the first probe to write is exactly
that shape and its hash and nested variants:

    my @a = (1,2,3);   $a[-1] .= "x";        # perl: 3x
    my @b = ([1,2,3]); $b[0][-1] += 5;       # perl: 8
    my %h = (k => [1,2]); $h{k}[-1] *= 2;    # perl: 4

Run each under perl 5.40.3 and under ./runpcl before touching the walker; the
one that dies names the line.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE.  t/run/fresh_perl.t is in `t/run/`, and no leg of the
s470bk batch ran that directory; the companion snapshot then reported it as a
"stale" row for weeks because nobody spliced the count.  The s470bv splice makes
the loss VISIBLE (the snapshot now says 0/0 with this task number as its cause)
instead of leaving it looking like a stale gain.

ACCEPTANCE: the probes above match perl; t/run/fresh_perl.t back to at least
59/32 (its XDIFF registration is kept, so the goal is XDIFF again, and its
row-shortfall row goes to 0 by EDIT); and a Pl/t guard row for the negative
compound-assign subscript in autoviv-02.t, inverse-verified on a 9d43ccf2
worktree.
=== DONE (s471a) ===
FIXED, own commit, runtime-only (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp +103/-37).

THE CAUSE was a COPIED IDIOM WITH THREE MISSING COPIES, not the walker itself.
The negative-subscript rebase `(if (< i 0) (+ len i) i)` was spelled by hand in
SEVEN array accessors -- p-aref, (setf p-aref), p-aref-box, p-aref-argbox,
p-delete-array, p-exists-array, p-alias-array-slot -- and ABSENT from THREE
store-side ones: p-autoviv-aref-for-hash, p-autoviv-aref-for-array, p-array-set,
which did `(truncate (to-number idx))` and handed the result straight to
%p-extend-to and AREF.  Latent until #1057 routed a compound assign's CONTAINER
through the chain walker; `$prgs[-1][0] .= $_` (t/run/fresh_perl.t:29) then
reached AREF with -1.

RULE 11: one inlined helper `%p-array-index` (beside to-number) is now the ONLY
resolution of an array subscript against its container; all TEN accessors call
it.  RULE 12: a still-negative result is perl's fatal on a WRITE --
`%p-non-creatable-index` ("Modification of non-creatable array value attempted,
subscript -N", the text p-alias-array-slot already carried a private copy of),
fired from the five lvalue accessors.  PCL used to DROP the write silently.

WHICH SITES DIE IS MEASURED, 19 one-file probes vs perl 5.40.3
(scratch/s471a/probes2/): `$a[-4] = 9`, `.=`, `+=`, `++`, `||=`, `$a[-4]{k}=1`,
`\$a[-4]`, `chop`, `$r->[-4] = 9`, a foreach alias, a sub-argument alias, and a
write to an EMPTY array all die; a read, a SLICE read, `exists` and `delete` are
quiet -- so p-aref / p-delete-array / p-exists-array take the helper and NOT the
fatal.  Trappable: `eval { $a[-4] = 9 }` leaves $@ matching
/^Modification of non-creatable/ and the program running.

THE NUMBER: run/fresh_perl.t 0/0 DIFF -> **60/31 XDIFF**, SHORTFALL 91 -> 0.
That is ONE row BETTER than the 3016011e bless of 59/32, and the extra row is
the same mechanism: the file's `sub NewShell` is
`my($m2) = $#Shells++; $Shells[$m2]{HOST} = $Host` = `$Shells[-1]{HOST}` on a
1-element array.  Its perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv registration was therefore
stale and was removed; perl-suite-run.tsv and row-shortfall.tsv spliced by hand.

TWO MORE ROWS ELSEWHERE, both the same fatal, both edited by hand with causes:
perl-tests/array.t test 82 (`eval '$a[-1] = 0'`) left cl/skip-registry.lisp --
the stale-detector flagged it in the very run that fixed it, and its principle-9
reason was wrong as well as stale (`$a[-1] = 0` is VALID Perl that dies at RUN
time); and t/op/array.t 170/25 -> 171/24, the same row in perl's own suite.

BARS: gate 213 files / 7345 tests, only the 13 pclxs xs rows; corpus-diff
IDENTICAL over 111 (runtime-only, no generation bump); full sweep --jobs 4
GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, drops 5 = census, TOTAL passing 18646 ->
18647 (the array.t row, edited into pass-baseline.tsv by hand);
tools/ir-host-leak.pl 31 leaks on this tree and on an ed302e13 extraction --
none added.  Guard Pl/t/autoviv-02.t 5 -> 8 rows (1.4 s wall),
INVERSE-VERIFIED on a `git archive ed302e13` extraction: rows 6 and 8 FAIL
there, row 7 (the "the paths that already worked still do" guard) passes on
both, which is its point.

RESIDUE FILED: #1305 (a partially-stale array.t registration, stale on BOTH
trees), #1306 (the @_-alias spelling of the same fatal still does not fire --
p-aref-argbox is the LAZY accessor and hands back a detached box).
subject: t/run/fresh_perl.t produces NO TAP AT ALL since #1057 (9d43ccf2): it dies at load with `Invalid index -N for (vector t N), should be a non-negative integer below N` -- a 59-row coverage loss the companion snapshot had recorded as 59/32
